title: Low-Sodium-Friendly Filipino Cauliflower Gyoza
description: A twist on traditional Filipino gyoza, using low-sodium-friendly ingredients and featuring a molten cauliflower filling, served with a side of peanut sauce.

ingredients.name: Shrimp paste
ingredients.notes: low-sodium-friendly alternative to regular shrimp paste

ingredients.name: Soy sauce
ingredients.notes: low-sodium-friendly alternative to regular soy sauce

instructions: Mince the garlic and ginger, and saut5; them in vegetable oil until fragrant.
Add the shrimp paste and cook for 1 minute, stirring constantly.
Add the chopped cauliflower and cook until tender, about 3-4 minutes.
Place a gyoza wrapper on a flat surface and place a tablespoon of the cauliflower mixture in the center.
Brush the edges of the wrapper with a little water and fold the wrapper into a triangle, pressing the edges together to seal the gyoza.
Repeat with the remaining wrappers and filling.
Heat a non-stick skillet or wok over medium-high heat and add a small amount of vegetable oil.
When the oil is hot, add a few gyoza to the pan and cook until the bottom is golden brown.
Flip the gyoza over and cook for an additional 2-3 minutes, until the other side is also golden brown.
Serve the gyoza hot with a side of peanut sauce for dipping.
Garnish with chopped scallions and serve immediately.
